learn.title: Big problems, small pieces
learn.body: Nobody writes a large program in one go. Programmers break a problem into small steps, solve each step, and then combine them. Functions are the natural way to hold the steps.

learn.title: A method
learn.body: First say the goal in one sentence. Then list the inputs and the output. Then write the steps in plain words, which is pseudocode. Only then write C. After each small piece, run it and check it before moving on.

learn.title: An example: leap years
learn.body: A year is a leap year if it divides by 400, or if it divides by 4 but not by 100. So 2000 and 2024 are leap years. 1900 is not, and neither is 2023. Our plan: check 400 first, then 100, then 4.

learn.title: From plan to code
learn.body: Each rule from the plan becomes one test. This is the function; `main` calls it.

learn.title: Checking 1900
steps: `1900 % 400` is 300, not 0, so the first test is skipped
`1900 % 100` is 0, so we return 0 straight away
1900 is not a leap year, which matches the rules

learn.title: Test with the edges
learn.body: Test normal values and the tricky ones. Here we tried 2000, 1900, 2024 and 2023: the program prints 1 0 1 0. Each result matches what the rules say. The tricky years exercise each branch.
The order of tests in the plan matters. Checking 4 first would wrongly call 1900 a leap year.

questions.prompt: What is a good first step when facing a big problem?
questions.explanation: Small steps can be solved and tested one at a time.

choices: A kind of comment that runs
questions.explanation: It helps you plan before the syntax gets in the way.

questions.prompt: Is 2024 a leap year? Type 1 for yes or 0 for no, as `is_leap` returns.
questions.explanation: 2024 divides by 4 and not by 100, so it is a leap year.
1900 divides by 100 but not by 400, so it is not a leap year.
2000 divides by 400, so it is a leap year.

questions.prompt: Why test with 1900 and 2000 as well as normal years?
questions.explanation: Edge cases reveal mistakes that ordinary values hide.

questions.prompt: Each small job in a program is often placed in its own \_\_.
questions.explanation: Functions give each step a name you can test.

questions.prompt: Put the problem-solving steps in order.
steps: State the goal in one sentence
questions.explanation: Plan first, then code, then check.
